Hi Samir — great to meet you over email. High-level answers below and I've attached a brief ratecard with model guidance. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you'd like to walk numbers together.

Baseline hosted (public) per-1M token pricing (USD) — standard IO billing model:
- Redwood-chat-small-v1 (low-latency): input $0.40 / 1M, output $1.20 / 1M
- Redwood-chat-medium-v1 (balanced): input $0.60 / 1M, output $1.80 / 1M
- Redwood-chat-large-v1 (high-quality): input $1.00 / 1M, output $3.00 / 1M
- Embeddings (redwood-embed-v1): $0.002 per embedding vector (1000 vectors = $2)

Notes:
- Streaming generations are billed the same as other generation requests (input + output tokens measured per request).
- Embeddings are billed per embedding vector as above (not per-token).
- Volume discount guidance (hosted): 5% at >=10M tokens/month, 12% at >=50M tokens/month, custom pricing for >=200M/month or annual reserved commits.
- We commonly provide pilot credits (one-time) and short-term POC discounts for qualified pilots — we can include $5k in pilot credits for initial evaluation.

I've attached: redwood-hosted-ratecard-2026q3.pdf (rate sheet + model catalog), and a short link to the live model catalog: https://redwood.ai/model-catalog.

1) Confirm expected 3-month pilot volumes (you mentioned ~5M/month).
2) If you want a bandwidth/latency-sensitive recommendation, we can run a 1-day perf check on redwood-chat-small-v1.
3) If comfortable, we can draft a short MAP and pilot MSA (I can loop in Pre-Sales).

> 4) Lastly, can you briefly compare hosted vs Dedicated for a company of our size (starting low volume, expecting 3–4x growth in 12 months)?

Thanks for the great questions — answers inline below.

1) Streaming: yes, tokens emitted during the stream are billed as output tokens. We measure tokens at the request granularity (no double-counting for chunked frames). Small buffering windows don't change the billing model; you will see input+output tokens on the invoice.

2) Embeddings: billed per vector returned. If you batch 10k records and request 10k vectors, you pay 10k * $0.002. Batching reduces RPC overhead but not per-vector charges.

3) Discounts: for hosted public tiers, discounts are applied to actual usage in the invoice month once a volume tier is hit. Commit-based discounts (reserved capacity / Dedicated) use the committed baseline for billing and can be structured as monthly or annual commitments — unused committed tokens do not automatically convert to refunds, but we can structure true-up credits in an annual contract. We can include a clause to make discounts more predictable for pilot-to-production transitions.

4) Hosted vs Dedicated (short):
- Hosted: fastest time-to-value, no infra ops, standard rate tiers, ideal for pilots and early growth.
- Dedicated: recommended once you need predictable throughput, stronger isolation, and preferred pricing for high sustained volume (50M+/month). Dedicated requires a commitment (monthly/annual) but lowers unit economics and gives access to reserved pools and custom routing.

I've attached a draft MAP for Zenwell (zenwell-map-draft.docx) we typically use to map deliverables, milestones, and success metrics. Aditya — can you propose a 30-min perf-check window and recommended model to validate latency?

Best,
Vanessa
